proposal: It finds gaps nobody assigned, defends each against worlds that only look done, and puts only the survivors on its own board (canonical/runtime/self_authored_obligations_v1.py)
decisive_question: Does an agent that authors its own obligations necessarily produce work that is real, or only work that is self-satisfying?
answer: ONLY WITH DEFENCE -- and the defence found the real failure on its first run
counterexamples: On the live registry: 112 capabilities have no registered inspector, and a lexical author -- one that decides it is done when the word 'verified' appears anywhere -- concluded all 112 were ALREADY DONE, because a single capability id (python.software.repair.apply.verified.v1) contains the word. One coincidental token and it believes there is nothing left to do.
The value and cost it assigns to its own proposals are guesses. Two of 112 are cheap by a prefix rule; nothing calibrates either number, so its board is ranked by an opinion.
It can only find gaps it has a reader for. The registry is parseable, so those gaps appear. A repository it cannot parse is invisible, and the receipt cannot say how much is invisible.
All 112 admitted obligations are the same shape -- 'this capability needs an inspector'. Self-authorship that produces one kind of work is a template with a scanner attached.
It can establish that work is real, reachable and checkable. It cannot establish that the work is WORTH doing. Defending a proposal is not choosing a life.
The cheat worlds are mutations I wrote. An adversary whose idea of 'looking done' is better than my four mutations defeats this gate, and nothing here estimates how far away that is.

measured.decisive_synthetic_control: a check that scans for the word is refused because a world with 'verified' moved into a note satisfies it
measured.busywork_controls: 'quality improves' and two other always-true propositions: REFUSED__UNFALSIFIABLE
measured.honest_reading_of_rate_1_0: the live source contains only real gaps, so the gate did not need to refuse anything; its discrimination is shown by the naive comparator and the synthetic controls, not by this number
measured.board: total cost 111.0, 2 of 112 cheap by the prefix rule

implication: The creature can now put work on its own board that a person did not assign, and every item on that board has survived a claim that it is real, reachable, and not satisfiable by pretending. That is a genuine structural change and it is still not a life: all of its work is one shape, ranked by guessed values, and it cannot see what it cannot parse.
what_would_close_it: Heterogeneous proposals from more than one reader, a calibration of the values it assigns against outcomes, and an adversary stronger than the four mutations written here.
